100.$description: 2. PRIMITIVES — Tidal (teal · primary · success) Anchored on the reference brand teal #14b8a6 at the 500 step.
4. PRIMITIVES — Plasma (magenta · accent · live data) Anchored on the reference brand magenta #f20084 at the 500 step.

sol.$description: PRIMITIVES — Sol (amber · caution · mid isoline bands)

3xs.$description: 8. SPACE — 4px base, semantic aliases for the rhythm layer Hand-picked steps, not a single ratio: the bottom half (0.25–1.25) serves component internals; the top half (1.75–5) is a ~1.4 ratio for page-level rhythm. A single ratio would not serve both.

scale.$description: 9. RADIUS — generously round, but not uniformly soft Driven by --radius-scale so a whole product can be tightened or softened from one value.

ring.$description: Ring geometry (one pitch for every circle in the system)

shadow.$description: Ring geometry (one pitch for every circle in the system)

control.$description: Target sizes by kind (WCAG 2.5.8). A control is pressed (44 px), a listbox option is selected (24 px), a chart control is 24 px, and a data mark is not a target at all.

mark.$description: a data mark is not a target

hue.$description: One hue drives the whole brand layer. Change it and every primary surface, ring and tint follows. The documented ramps above stay fixed, so the palette reference never drifts.

control-edge.$description: Control edge: the border of an input, select, textarea or secondary/outline button. Must clear 3:1 against every surface it can sit on (WCAG 1.4.11). The binding surface is --color-surface-3 in both themes: at the previous 62%/56% the edge measured 3.01:1 light and 2.84:1 dark there, so the dark step failed the contract this comment states. 61%/58% measures 3.14 and 3.09 — the smallest change that clears 3:1 with margin, chosen by sweeping the same canvas estimator the gate certifies with.

primary-solid.$description: Filled surfaces need one extra step of depth so white text clears 4.5:1 on a light background.

heat-1.$description: NOT a sequential ramp: luminance is not monotonic across the six steps. Use --chart-seq-* for any ordered band.

density.$description: A single multiplier that compresses row padding and gaps, so the same table can serve a 34-inch analyst monitor and an embedded widget. 1 = comfortable, 0.72 = compact.

1.$description: Categorical — eight series, ordered so neighbouring hues stay apart. Cap at eight: past that, adjacent colours stop being reliably distinguishable and the tail should fold into "other". Closest pairs by luminance (C-20, measured): light 2↔8 (ΔL .0053), dark 1↔5 (ΔL .0001, ratio 1.00). Series 1 stays the default (brand hue) by design; separation is reported, not gated, and the dash pattern discharges WCAG 1.4.1. No reordering performed.

cyc-1.$description: Cyclic — equal lightness, hue carries the encoding, wraps seamlessly. For bearing/aspect/phase/time-of-day data where 0 and 360 are the same value: index mod N, so the last stop meets the first. The seam is a neutral (low chroma) so the wrap reads as continuous rather than as a hard edge.

ticks.$description: The chart's tick count, and the reason the grid can align at all. Gridlines are one repeating band, so a band is exactly `100% / (ticks - 1)` wide and every line falls on a tick by construction — see `.c-chart__plot`. An author sets this to the number of labels their axis actually renders; `Contour.chart.ticks()` returns that many values. Five is the CSS convention, not a ceiling.

tip-block-start.$description: Where a tooltip sits inside its plot. Declared here rather than invented at the point of use: a `var()` reference to a token that exists nowhere is the exact discrepancy `node tools/check-tokens.mjs` fails the build on, and a consumer overriding an undeclared knob gets nothing. Both default to the plot's own origin, so a tooltip with no anchors is still positioned.

label.$description: Axis labels are text, not furniture: --type-micro is below the large-text exemption, so this must clear the same 4.5:1 body copy does. Measured, the dark value sat at 4.23:1 on --color-surface-3 (basalt-800) — the one surface in the set it failed — which is why the floor is 70% and not 66%.

attribution-inset-block.$description: The attribution band (C-15). A map's credit line is the one piece of chrome a consumer does not own: the vendor's terms say it must be visible over the map, and let us choose its colour and size but not its presence. So the geometry lives here rather than in the rule, because a dashboard that wants the bottom-right corner has to move the band, and moving a token is a reviewable act while overriding a rule is not. The logo box is the size the vendor ships — 65px by 20px, published in their own CSS — and it is a MINIMUM: the band reserves room for the mark and never resizes it.

com.contour.version.deprecation: A deprecated token keeps its name and gains a `$deprecated` boolean plus a `replacement` pointer in its `$extensions`; removals land in the next major release (see CHANGELOG.md).

com.contour.dtcg.statement: Generated by tools/build.mjs; src/css stays the source of truth. The tokens named here are declared CSS the Format Module cannot represent, so a consumer must read the stylesheet for them — they are listed rather than dropped, and tools/check-export.mjs fails unless exported plus refused equals the census. Note what this document CANNOT say: a knob-resolved colour is published at the value :root declares, so the JSON describes the default theme only. Re-pointing --brand-hue works from :root and not from a subtree — that is why .c-theme-scope re-derives the whole brand layer rather than overriding one value — and a Resolver set carries themes, not an arbitrary hue. Read src/css for the mechanism.

fluid-value.because: clamp()/min()/max() resolve per viewport, so there is no single value to publish

unit-not-expressible (em).because: the Format Module allows only px and rem; the declared length is in another unit

unit-not-expressible (ch).because: the Format Module allows only px and rem; the declared length is in another unit

composite-value (light-dark() inside a c.because: a computed expression over other tokens, or a multi-part value (a shadow list, a length with a style), that is not one typed value

value-not-classified (linear).because: the exporter reached the end of its rules without a type — treat as a defect

alias-target-refused (--gutter).because: the token it aliases is itself refused, so a reference would dangle

colour-not-parseable (knob substitution.because: not a colour literal this exporter can read without guessing

dash-list.because: strokeStyle needs a lineCap that a dash token never states; inventing one would be a new claim

gradient-value.because: a CSS gradient is not the array of stops the gradient type requires
